ai.description: This 5–8 cm frog is typically yellowish-brown with dark dorsal stripes. It features a pointed snout, granular skin, and distinct webbing on the feet. It is a member of the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates leucomystax* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale line running along the upper lip, which is absent in similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: The Java Whipping Frog inhabits moist deciduous forests, plantations, and rural gardens, typically found at low to moderate elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Java whipping frog is primarily nocturnal, often congregating near water bodies at night to engage in loud, rhythmic choruses for mating.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates leucomystax* breeds during the monsoon, laying 100–400 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Polypedates leucomystax* is found in Northeast India, primarily across the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, and Meghalaya, typically at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Java Whipping Frog emits a series of sharp, rhythmic "chack-chack" notes at a high pitch, typically heard from vegetation surrounding ponds or marshes.
